problems.title: Where is my planet?
problems.statement: The attached map shows the sky as it could be observed at 13:00 UT of November 8, 2021, if no atmosphere was present, from a locality on the Earth located at longitude $\lambda=0^\circ$ and latitude $\varphi$. The positions of the Sun and of the Moon (as a small sickle) are shown. In the map planets Jupiter, Mars, Mercury, Saturn and Venus are also visible, represented with dots whose dimension is proportional to their current luminosity.

figures.alt: Complete circular sky map with all compass and degree labels, the labelled Sun and Moon, and the empty latitude box at upper right.
figures.caption: Round on Maps and Images. Map for problem 10

parts.statement: Estimate the latitude $\varphi$ of the place where observation could be made and write it in degrees inside the box on right top of the map.
Draw on the map as a dotted line the ecliptic and identify with “**Ecl**”.
Draw on the map as a continuous line the celestial equator and identify with “**Eqt**”.
Identify on the map the planets and indicate them with their standard designation (like ☿, ♀, ♁, ♂, ♃, ♄, ♅, ♆).

Identify on the map the following 14 constellation, writing their three letter code nearby:

**Aql, Boo, Cen, Cru, Crv, Del, Her, Leo, Lib, Lyr, Oph, Sgr, TrA, Vir**.

Identify on the map the following 5 stars, writing the indicated three digit code nearby:

Acrux (**Acr**), Albireo (**Alb**), Antares (**Ant**), Denebola (**Den**), Mizar (**Miz**).

problems.title: Who is who?
problems.statement:
You are provided with a sheet where images of 12 astronomical objects are shown. Identify these objects marking the correct answer among the listed four. Multiple choose or corrections are not allowed.

[[figure twelve-object-sheet-astra-root4-20260925]]

*[Transcription note: the row and column positions below identify the photographs in the original sheet. All choices are reproduced in their printed order.]*

| Image position | Printed choices |
|---|---|
| Row 1, left | Hyperion; Comet P/1; Mimas; Enceladus |
| Row 1, centre | Halley comet; Comet P/47; Comet P/67; Hale-Bopp comet |
| Row 1, right | Moon (far side); Ganymede; Mercury; Callisto |
| Row 2, left | Calypso; Deimos; Phobos; Amalthea |
| Row 2, centre | Miranda; Ariel; Umbriel; Titania |
| Row 2, right | Nereid; Mimas; Triton; Pluto |
| Row 3, left | M1; M31; M45; M101 |
| Row 3, centre | M1; M31; M45; M101 |
| Row 3, right | M1; M45; M31; M101 |
| Row 4, left | M1; M31; M45; M101 |
| Row 4, centre | Comet Tempel 1; Comet P/67; Comet Tempel 2; Comet P/47 |
| Row 4, right | Orcus; Vesta; Charon; Pluto |
